messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Performance SLO & context window follow-up

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have the alignment and next steps.

Highlights from the call:
- Primary goal: power FinCo’s real-time assistant inside your trading portal with strict latency SLOs and streaming of partial results.
- Target latency: p95 <= 200ms for typical flows; p50 target we discussed ~80–120ms.
- Context window: typical input is 1k–2k tokens (user prompt + recent convo), output average ~150–400 tokens. Peak long-form use cases can hit ~4k input + output ~1k.
- Concurrency/throughput: initial traffic estimate ~50–100 rps, but burst concurrency up to 200 concurrent sessions during market open.
- Streaming: yes — you need early token streaming (low startup time) for responsiveness.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 and audit logs required; you mentioned procurement will want standard SLAs and a data-handling addendum.

Open clarifications we need from you to size the perf run and proposal:
1) For the SLOs above, is p95 <= 200ms an absolute requirement for all query lengths, or for the 1k–2k typical case?
2) Expected % of requests that exceed 2k tokens (so we can plan GPU memory/kv cache).
3) Do you require streaming for every request type, or only for the interactive assistant flows?
4) Any hard limits on startup time (e.g., speech-to-text style startup <= 80ms)?

Next steps (proposed):
- I’ll send a short SLO proposal and a latency test plan (attached) that outlines the staged perf run we recommend (staging token distributions, concurrency sweep, and streaming latency measurements).
- We can run a benchmark against a representative sample or synthetic traces. We estimate initial perf run results within 7 business days once we have a staging endpoint and sample payloads.
- Follow-up call to review results + recommended model/quantization config.

Attachments: SLO-proposal-FinCo.pdf (proposal + pricing/committed throughput), latency-test-plan.xlsx (test matrix).

Would you be able to confirm answers to the 4 clarifying questions above and a preferred time window for the perf run next week?

Best,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

---
Note: For the perf run we typically test 2 model variants: a high-quality 70B-family run (quantized) and a 13B low-latency variant; we also include streaming latency (time-to-first-byte) and end-to-end p50/p95/p99 token latency in the report.

From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@finco.com>

Cc: FinCo Procurement <procurement@finco.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:42:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & context window follow-up

Thanks Marissa — nice summary. A few answers and clarifications from our side:

- p95 <= 200ms is a hard requirement for the interactive assistant flows (the ones embedded in the trading UI). For batch workflows we can tolerate higher tail latency.
- Typical distribution: ~70% of requests are 1k–2k input tokens with ~150 tokens output. ~20% are short (<500 tokens). ~10% are long-form (3–5k combined).
- Streaming: required for interactive assistant (priority). For notifications/batch jobs we don’t need streaming.
- Startup time: we’d like time-to-first-byte (TTFB) <= 100ms if possible for interactive sessions; <80ms would be ideal but understand that may be challenging for longer contexts.

We can provide a 48-hour staging window and a sample payload set next week. Procurement will follow up on SLA language — I copied the procurement alias.

Can you confirm what model family and quantization level you expect to hit p95 <= 200ms for the 1k–2k case, and what hardware (GPU type) you plan to run the perf sweep on?

Thanks,
Sarah Lee
Product Lead, Conversational AI | FinCo

Vivek / Rishi — noting Sarah’s clarifications below and proposing the perf plan. Copying FinCo for visibility.

Key takeaways from Sarah: p95 <= 200ms hard for interactive flows; TTFB target <= 100ms (ideal <80ms); token distribution heavy on 1k–2k.

Recommended perf run plan (short):
1) Models to test: 
   - redwood-mosaic-70b (4-bit quantized, CPU/GPU mixed kernels) — quality-focused; expect higher latency for 4k contexts unless we use KV cache + sharded KV placement.
   - redwood-stream-13b (optimized low-latency variant, 4-bit) — lower mem footprint, better single-GPU tail latency.
2) Hardware: start with NVIDIA H100 (single-GPU runs to measure TTFB and p50/p95; then multi-GPU distributed for concurrency sweep). We should also include an A100 run since FinCo may prefer marketplace SKUs.
3) Test matrix (see latency-test-plan.xlsx): token distributions (short/typical/long), concurrency sweep [1,5,10,20,50,100], streaming on/off, batching policies (no batching for interactive; microbatching for throughput runs), and TTFB measurement (time to first token).
4) Kernels/optimizations: enable prefix KV caching for session continuity, use continuous batching for high throughput tests, and enable int4/ql4 quantization when possible.
5) Acceptance criteria: for typical case (1k–2k input + 150 output) p95 <= 200ms and TTFB <= 100ms on the low-latency 13B variant (or a quantized 70B if we can demonstrate similar numbers).

Initial capacity estimate: with the 13B low-latency variant on a single H100 we expect ~30–50 rps for the 1k–2k flows with p95 in target; 70B will be lower throughput (~8–12 rps) but higher quality. These are rough until we run the sweep.

Action items:
- Rishi: please spin up a staging cluster (H100 + A100 nodes) and provision a temporary endpoint. Use the payload set Sarah will provide.
- Vivek: coordinate scheduling with FinCo and confirm the 48-hour staging window.
- Marissa: run the initial streaming latency tests and share the results + dashboard.

Sarah — can you drop the payload set (sample traces + token distribution) into the Drive link I shared in the related_links? I’ll prioritize the streaming TTFB measurements first.

Thanks,
Marissa
